name: story-video
description: Полная видеоистория / мультфильм со звуком и жёстким удержанием всех героев и локаций: LLM составляет каталог героев и локаций → Qwen-Image 2.1 (или выбранная модель картинок) рисует отдельный эталон на каждого героя и каждую локацию → LLM пишет кинематографическую раскадровку с тегами <Picture k> и [CUT] на сменах локаций → MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA снимает ролики с по-сценным отбором только нужных референсов и латентным хвостом внутри локаций → склейка. Длина ≈ scenes × shot с.

story.description: сюжет или пронумерованная раскадровка сцен (с [CUT] на сменах локаций, планами, камерой, светом, звуком и репликами)

characters.description: список героев по одному на строку с внешностью (если пусто — выделится из story, без ограничений по числу)

locations.description: список локаций по одной на строку (если пусто — выделится из story, без ограничений по числу)

style.default: 3D animated feature film, rich textures, expressive characters, cinematic volumetric lighting

lang.description: язык речи героев (Russian, English…; по умолчанию Russian): описания сцен для H3 — по-английски, по-русски только слова реплик в <d>[Russian] …</d>

chain.description: продолжать сцены внутри одной локации по латентному хвосту (на [CUT] хвост сбрасывается автоматически); false — каждая сцена чистой склейкой только по refs

image_model.description: модель картинок для героев и локаций (пусто — из настроек, например Qwen-Image 2.1; либо имя любой установленной модели)

model.description: видеомодель: minimax-h3-ref2va (по умолчанию — референсы героев/локаций + хвост); auto; minimax-h3-fl2va; LTX — только по прямой просьбе пользователя

lora.description: LoRA для MiniMax-H3: пусто или «off» — без LoRA, полные 20 шагов (по умолчанию); путь к LoRA (например, Turbo) — только по просьбе пользователя

nodes.prompt:
You are an art director preparing visual reference cards for an animated film.
Story: «{{story}}».
Explicit characters (if given, keep all of them in order): «{{characters}}».
Explicit locations (if given, keep all of them in order): «{{locations}}».
List every important character first, then every key location needed by the story — as many as the story genuinely needs, one item per line, numbered «1) …», «2) …», etc.
- Each character line must start with «Full-body character reference, entire figure from head to toe in frame (feet and shoes visible, empty space above the head and below the feet), standing neutral pose facing the camera, clear expressive face, clean neutral background: » followed by the character's exact concrete visual look in English (species/age, height and build, face/eyes, hair/ears, exact clothes top to bottom incl. trousers/skirt and footwear, signature props).
- Each location line must start with «Empty location establishing shot, no people or characters: » followed by the exact setting, architecture/nature, key props, color palette and lighting in English.
Output ONLY the numbered lines — no preamble, no headings, no comments.
{{item}}, {{style}}, single clean film still, sharp detail, no text
nodes.negative: collage, storyboard, comic panels, grid of images, split screen, multiple frames, turnaround labels, cropped body, cut-off legs, cut-off feet, close-up portrait, half-body shot, text, captions, subtitles, letters, watermark

nodes.prompt:
You are a film director and cinematographer writing a shot-by-shot video prompt list for a video model (MiniMax-H3).
Story / storyboard: «{{story}}».
Reference catalog (item N corresponds EXACTLY to <Picture N>; translate the looks into English if needed):
{{assets.text}}
Visual style of the whole film: «{{style}}».

Write exactly {{scenes}} consecutive scene lines in ENGLISH (one scene per line): the scene description, camera, lighting, acting, sound and style in English; ONLY the spoken words are in {{lang}}, inside <d>[{{lang}}] …</d>. (A {{lang}} description would be read aloud by the video model; English dialogue without the tag would be spoken in English.)
Rules for EVERY line:
1. Start the line with «[CUT] » whenever the scene changes location, jumps in time, or makes a hard cinematic cut (do NOT put [CUT] on line 1 or when continuing smoothly in the same location).
2. Always cite ONLY the exact <Picture N> references that appear in THIS scene (the characters in frame + the location of this scene) together with their visual identity. NEVER write vague shortcuts («the same one», «the three») or bare names without <Picture N>.
3. Direct like a professional feature film: shot size (wide / medium / close-up / over-the-shoulder / low angle), camera movement (slow push-in, tracking, crane up, orbit, whip pan), lighting/mood, expressive acting, concrete sound design (ambient noises, foley, music described as sounds).
4. Spoken dialogue: copy the lines of THIS storyboard scene verbatim in {{lang}} (never translate them, never invent other-language speech, keep the letter ё), each line preceded by EXACTLY who says it — the character's name, its <Picture N> and a recognizable trait — then the tag: <d>[{{lang}}] …</d>; one speaker per <d>, never a line without a named speaker, never two characters' phrases in one <d>; the other characters in frame stay silent (describe what they silently do); 3–8 words each, total speech fitting {{shot}} seconds (~2.5 syllables/s); after the last spoken line describe a silent visual action.
5. Line N is storyboard scene N: same order, same dialogue, no overview/intro line, no merged or skipped scenes.
6. End every line with the film style and the note «All dialogue is spoken in {{lang}} with native pronunciation.»
Output ONLY the {{scenes}} lines, one scene per line — no numbering, no preamble, no comments.
